transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just can’t seem to stop launching projects. It's like I have to do everything right now. I'm rolling out all these massive new work plans and certification schedules for my team, and then at home, I'm doing a complete network upgrade. I actually just ripped out all the old Cat5e cabling in the walls to put in Cat6a because I wanted the 10-gigabit throughput. I was talking to this guy at the electronics store about it, and he didn't even know the difference between the shielding types, which is just... I mean, how do you work in that department and not know? 

So I ended up messaging a bunch of old contacts from my bachelor's program to see what they were running at their houses. We used to hang out at this terrible diner near campus that had the absolute worst coffee, but they stayed open 24 hours, so we'd just sit there and code until sunrise... 

Anyway, sorry, what was I saying? Right, the projects. I just keep starting all these things—the network, the messages, the schedules. It gets so intense that I just blow past normal limits. I don't even realize how far I've gone until my wife or my IT director at work has to actually step in and make me stop.

Have you noticed any time recently when your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt extremely confident or energetic, even to the point where others might have noticed something was different about you?

Yeah, actually... there are these weeks where I just feel, I don't know, almost electric. Like I'm completely unstoppable. I'll be flying through all these things I need to do, and I just feel this incredible surge of energy. But then, if there's even a tiny delay, or if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm doing, I just... I snap. It feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down on purpose, you know? 

Which is ridiculous because my wife, she's usually so patient. We met back when I was still finishing my bachelor's, actually. She was studying graphic design and she used to make these incredible digital portraits. She did one of me once, but she lost the file when her old hard drive crashed. I told her she should have been using a RAID setup for redundancy, which is exactly why I'm so obsessed with the network upgrades now. You can't just trust a single point of failure. I mean, the amount of data we generate every day... 

Wait, did that answer your question? I was talking about feeling electric, right? Yeah, it's just... I get so high-energy, and then I just get so irritable if anyone gets in my way.

Can you describe a specific time when you noticed your mood was distinctly different from usual — like being unusually upbeat, wired, or irritable — and if this affected your behavior in a significant way?

Yeah, like... well, during those electric weeks I was just talking about, I literally cannot sit still. It's like my body is vibrating. I’ll pace around the house with my laptop just typing away, then suddenly I'm out reorganizing the garage, and then I'm back inside rewriting all my project boards for work. If my wife suggests we just sit and watch a show, I get physically uncomfortable. My skin just crawls. 

Actually, we tried to watch that new sci-fi series the other night. The one with the space station? The CGI was terrible, though. The way they rendered the zero-gravity physics was completely inaccurate. It reminded me of this physics class I took in my sophomore year. The professor was this older guy who always wore these ridiculous bow ties, like, every single day a different pattern. I think he got them custom-made. He had this whole collection... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the show. Yeah, I couldn't even make it through ten minutes of the pilot. I just had to get up and start moving again. I just can't stop doing things when I get like that.

Can you recall if there was a specific period — days or more — when your mood was consistently different from usual, like being unusually high, overly confident, or extremely irritable, to the point where people close to you might have said you were acting out of character?

Yeah, for sure. When I get into one of those stretches where I'm just buzzing, it's not just the energy... it's like my brain is working on a completely different level. I get this absolute certainty that I'm the only person who can actually see the whole architecture clearly. Like, the whole system. And I honestly believe that if people would just get out of my way and follow my plan exactly, I could save the company from a major failure. 

Because, honestly, the way they have the legacy servers set up right now is a disaster waiting to happen. I keep telling my IT director that we need to migrate everything to a cloud-based hybrid model, but he’s so stuck in his ways. He reminds me of this guy I used to buy comic books from when I was a kid. He ran this dusty little shop downtown and he refused to use a barcode scanner. He literally memorized the price of every single issue in the store. He had these huge binders behind the counter... 

Anyway... what was the question? Oh, right, acting out of character. Yeah, my wife definitely notices. She says I get really intense and start acting like I know better than everyone else. But in those moments, I really feel like I do.

Can you recall if there was a time when this intense, high-energy mood lasted for several days in a row — like four or more days — without completely going away, even if it got better for a few hours here or there?

Four days? I mean... I don't really keep a calendar or track the exact number of days when it happens. It just feels like one long, continuous stretch, to be honest. Time gets really blurry when I'm in the zone like that. 

It's kind of like when you're running a massive data migration and you're just staring at the terminal watching the command lines scroll by. You completely lose track of the hours. Actually, I bought this custom mechanical keyboard specifically for those long stretches. It has these really heavy, clicky switches. My wife absolutely hates the sound of it, though. She says it sounds like a hailstorm inside the home office. I actually tried installing these little rubber O-rings under the keycaps to quiet it down for her, but it completely ruined the tactile feedback. The whole point of those switches is feeling that exact moment of actuation, you know? If it feels mushy, you might as well just use a cheap membrane keyboard from the nineties... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? You asked about how long it lasts, right? Yeah, I'm honestly not sure if it's exactly four days or more or what. I just don't really count the days when I'm buzzing like that.
Can you think of a time when this high-energy, intense mood was present for at least four days straight — meaning it didn’t just come and go, but was consistently there for several days?

Yeah, definitely. When I get into those stretches—like I was saying, it just feels like one continuous thing. Some weeks I feel almost electric, you know? Completely unstoppable. Like I could just power through anything. But then... it's weird, because I'm so up and energized, but if my wife asks me a simple question, or if there's even a tiny delay in what I'm doing, I just snap. 

It feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down on purpose. Like they're dragging their feet just to mess with my momentum. It's so frustrating. It's like when you're driving on the highway and you're making great time, and then some guy in a Prius just parks himself in the left lane going exactly the speed limit. I had that happen last month when I was driving down to visit my brother. He lives near the coast, and the drive is usually beautiful, but this one guy just would not move over. I flashed my lights, I honked, nothing. It's like people have zero situational awareness these days. They just live in their own little bubbles. My brother's actually thinking about moving, though. The property taxes down there are getting insane. He was looking at a place in Nevada...

Sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, the mood. It's like that—electric and unstoppable, but I get so incredibly irritable if anyone gets in my way. And yeah, that feeling definitely lasts for days at a time.

Can you confirm if there was a time when this intense, high-energy mood stayed with you every day for at least four full days in a row, without going away completely, even if it got a little better for a few hours at a time?

I mean, like I said, I don't sit there with a calendar checking off the days. It's not like I have a stopwatch running. It just feels like a really long stretch where I'm completely wired and everything is moving at lightspeed, but everyone else is stuck in molasses. 

It's actually kind of like how they run sprints in agile development, you know? You have this set period where you're just burning through tasks, except in my head, the sprint never actually ends. We just switched to a new project management software at work, actually. Jira was getting too clunky, so we moved to this newer platform, but honestly, the UI is terrible. The color scheme alone gives me a headache. It's all these washed-out pastels. Who designs a productivity app with pastels? It looks like a baby shower invitation. I told the vendor that on our last Zoom call, and I think I really offended their lead designer. He got super quiet and turned his camera off. But I mean, someone had to say it, right? If you're charging enterprise rates, you should at least give us a dark mode that doesn't look like an Easter egg...

Wait, sorry. Four days. You keep asking about four days. I just... I don't know if it's exactly four days. It's just a long time. I don't track it like that.

Can you think back and confirm if there was ever a time when you felt this intense, high-energy mood every single day for four days or more—so not just coming and going, but clearly present day after day without stopping, even if it got a little better for a few hours at times?

Look, I know you really want me to give you an exact number. Like I said earlier, yes, it definitely goes on for days at a time. Sometimes whole weeks where I'm just electric, totally unstoppable. And it stays like that day after day. But then, like I was saying about my wife, if she just asks a simple question or if there's even a tiny delay in whatever I'm doing, I just snap. It genuinely feels like everyone is deliberately trying to slow me down on purpose. 

Speaking of things slowing me down on purpose, my internet provider has been throttling my bandwidth all week. I pay for symmetric gigabit, but the node in our neighborhood is clearly oversubscribed. I actually set up a Raspberry Pi on my home network just to run automated speed tests every fifteen minutes so I have a paper trail to send to the FCC. I swear, telecom companies get away with murder in this country. It's exactly like the airlines. You buy a ticket, they overbook the flight, and then they try to bribe you with a cheap voucher to fly out the next day. I got stuck in Atlanta once for fourteen hours because of that. The food court there is a total ripoff, too. A basic turkey sandwich was like fourteen dollars, and the bread was totally stale... 

Wait, did I answer your question? You're asking about the four days thing again, right? Yeah, it's definitely present day after day without stopping like that. I just don't tally it up on a calendar.

Can you confirm whether there was a time when you felt this intense, high-energy mood every single day for at least four days in a row—meaning it was clearly present each day without going away completely, even if it got a little better for a few hours at a time?

I mean, yes, I've said this, right? It's like I was telling you, there are some weeks where I just feel completely electric. Totally unstoppable, day after day. It doesn't just turn off. But then, you know, it's the smallest things that set me off. My wife will ask me something simple, or there's just this tiny delay in whatever I'm doing, and I just snap. It really feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down on purpose. 

Which, honestly, is exactly what happened at the grocery store yesterday. I was just trying to get some coffee beans—the whole bean kind, not the pre-ground stuff because it loses all its flavor within like, a day of opening the bag. Anyway, the self-checkout line was completely backed up because this one woman was trying to scan a massive bag of dog food by holding it up to the little laser instead of using the hand scanner. It’s like, the hand scanner is literally right there. It has a bright green button. How do you miss that? I swear, user experience design in retail environments is completely broken. They build these systems assuming everyone has a baseline level of technical literacy, but they don't. It’s like when my mom tries to use her iPad and ends up accidentally subscribing to five different streaming services. I spent three hours on the phone with customer support last Thanksgiving trying to get her refunds. The hold music was this awful, looping jazz track that sounded like it was recorded underwater... 

But yeah, anyway, the mood. It's like that. Electric, unstoppable for weeks, but I snap if anyone gets in my way. It doesn't just go away.

Was there a time when you felt this way — unusually energetic, wired, or irritable — every single day for at least four days in a row, without the feeling going away completely, even if it got a little better for a few hours at a time?

Look, I feel like we're going in circles with the four days thing. Like I keep saying, yes, it doesn't just go away. These stretches where I'm unusually driven, barely needing any sleep, and just feeling completely overconfident... they've been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. 

Actually, a year and eight months is exactly when I bought my current car. It's an EV, and honestly, the whole range anxiety thing you hear about is completely overblown by the media. I commute forty miles a day and just plug it into a standard wall outlet at night. You don't even need the expensive 240-volt installation unless you're driving cross-country every weekend. The real problem is the infotainment system. It runs on this proprietary Linux build that hasn't had an over-the-air update since the day I drove it off the lot. I actually tried to root it last weekend so I could sideload some better navigation apps, but they completely locked down the bootloader. Why do companies do that? You buy the hardware, you should own it, right? It's exactly like John Deere locking farmers out of repairing their own tractors. The whole right-to-repair movement is really gaining traction, though. I signed a petition for it last month because if I want to swap out a battery on my phone, I shouldn't have to melt the adhesive with a heat gun just to get inside the casing... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, the wired stretches. It's been about a year and eight months of this.

I actually set up a Raspberry Pi on my home network just to run automated speed tests every fifteen minutes so I have a paper trail to send to the FCC. I swear, telecom companies get away with murder in this country. It's exactly like the airlines. You buy a ticket, they overbook the flight, and then they try to bribe you with a cheap voucher to fly out the next day. I got stuck in Atlanta once for fourteen hours because of that. The food court there is a total ripoff, too. A basic turkey sandwich was like fourteen dollars, and the bread was totally stale... 

Wait, did I answer your question? You're asking about the four days thing again, right? Yeah, it's definitely present day after day without stopping like that. I just don't tally it up on a calendar.

doctor.intent: Confirm whether the patient has experienced a distinct period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood lasting at least 4 consecutive days, which is a key criterion for differentiating between bipolar disorder subtypes.
doctor.question: Can you confirm whether there was a time when you felt this intense, high-energy mood every single day for at least four days in a row—meaning it was clearly present each day without going away completely, even if it got a little better for a few hours at a time?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Some weeks I feel almost electric and unstoppable, but then a tiny delay or a question from my wife can make me snap like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to confirm the duration of the intense, high-energy (elevated/irritable) mood, which directly corresponds to this symptom.

patient.answer:
I mean, yes, I've said this, right? It's like I was telling you, there are some weeks where I just feel completely electric. Totally unstoppable, day after day. It doesn't just turn off. But then, you know, it's the smallest things that set me off. My wife will ask me something simple, or there's just this tiny delay in whatever I'm doing, and I just snap. It really feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down on purpose. 

Which, honestly, is exactly what happened at the grocery store yesterday. I was just trying to get some coffee beans—the whole bean kind, not the pre-ground stuff because it loses all its flavor within like, a day of opening the bag. Anyway, the self-checkout line was completely backed up because this one woman was trying to scan a massive bag of dog food by holding it up to the little laser instead of using the hand scanner. It’s like, the hand scanner is literally right there. It has a bright green button. How do you miss that? I swear, user experience design in retail environments is completely broken. They build these systems assuming everyone has a baseline level of technical literacy, but they don't. It’s like when my mom tries to use her iPad and ends up accidentally subscribing to five different streaming services. I spent three hours on the phone with customer support last Thanksgiving trying to get her refunds. The hold music was this awful, looping jazz track that sounded like it was recorded underwater... 

But yeah, anyway, the mood. It's like that. Electric, unstoppable for weeks, but I snap if anyone gets in my way. It doesn't just go away.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a distinct period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood lasting at least 4 consecutive days, as required for a manic or hypomanic episode, which helps differentiate between F31.4 (Bipolar I disorder, current episode manic without psychotic features), F31.1 (Bipolar II disorder), and F31.8 (Other specified bipolar disorders).
doctor.question: Was there a time when you felt this way — unusually energetic, wired, or irritable — every single day for at least four days in a row, without the feeling going away completely, even if it got a little better for a few hours at a time?

target_item.name: Manic Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The unusually driven, low-sleep, overconfident stretches have been part of my life for roughly 1 year and 8 months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the duration of the unusually energetic and irritable periods, so I will provide the total duration of these manic stretches.

patient.answer:
Look, I feel like we're going in circles with the four days thing. Like I keep saying, yes, it doesn't just go away. These stretches where I'm unusually driven, barely needing any sleep, and just feeling completely overconfident... they've been a part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. 

Actually, a year and eight months is exactly when I bought my current car. It's an EV, and honestly, the whole range anxiety thing you hear about is completely overblown by the media. I commute forty miles a day and just plug it into a standard wall outlet at night. You don't even need the expensive 240-volt installation unless you're driving cross-country every weekend. The real problem is the infotainment system. It runs on this proprietary Linux build that hasn't had an over-the-air update since the day I drove it off the lot. I actually tried to root it last weekend so I could sideload some better navigation apps, but they completely locked down the bootloader. Why do companies do that? You buy the hardware, you should own it, right? It's exactly like John Deere locking farmers out of repairing their own tractors. The whole right-to-repair movement is really gaining traction, though. I signed a petition for it last month because if I want to swap out a battery on my phone, I shouldn't have to melt the adhesive with a heat gun just to get inside the casing... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, the wired stretches. It's been about a year and eight months of this.

inference.note: The patient confirmed experiencing persistent high-energy, irritable, and overconfident mood states lasting for extended periods (approximately a year and eight months), consistent with Bipolar I Disorder, Current Episode Manic, Moderate.
